newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BLINKER BANNED WORLDWIDE BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLINKER BANNED WORLDWIDE BY FIFA.

text.p: Sheffield Wednesday's Dutch forward Regi Blinker has been handed a worldwide suspension by FIFA for allegedly signing two contracts within months of each other.

Blinker, 27, joined the English premier league club from Feyenoord in March for 250,000 pounds ($420,000) but Italian side Udinese say he signed a document two months earlier pledging himself to play for them this season.
"We want to find out why he seemed to sign contracts with different clubs, one in England and one in Italy," a FIFA spokesman said.
He said Blinker, who has appeared in every match Sheffield Wednesday have played this season, has been asked to supply soccer's world governing body with an explanation by next Friday.
"The ban applies until then at least and perhaps beyond," the spokesman said.
The English Football Association has appealed to FIFA to lift the ban until Blinker has had time to respond, and Wednesday said they were being wrongly punished.
"The suspension is totally unfair on Sheffield Wednesday," club secretary Graham Mackerell said. "We are totally innocent, as are Feyenoord.
"This is purely a matter between Regi and Udinese. A suspension punishes Sheffield Wednesday but there is no suggestion that we have done anything wrong."
Blinker was in Wednesday's squad for their match at Sunderland on Saturday.
